title: Percentages and fraction–decimal–percent conversion
summary: Per cent means "out of a hundred". Use a hundred square and a 100% bar to see that a fraction, a decimal and a percentage are three names for one amount.
guide: {{term:percent}} means "out of 100". 16% is 16 out of 100: {{frac:16/100}}, or {{num:0.16}}.
A hundred square has 100 small squares. Each one is {{frac:1/100}}, or 1%. Each column of 10 is {{frac:1/10}}, or 10%.
A whole bar is 100% of something. Split it into 10 parts and each part is 10%. To turn a fraction into a percentage, make an equivalent fraction with a denominator of 10 or 100.

hundred-square.title: {{num:0.3}} on a hundred square
hundred-square.prompt: This square has 100 small squares. First predict: how many small squares is {{num:0.3}}? Then shade {{num:0.3}} of the square.
hundred-square.hint: {{num:0.3}} is 3 {{term:tenth}}s. Each column of 10 small squares is one tenth.
hundred-square.success: Well done! 30 out of 100 squares are shaded: {{num:0.3}} = {{frac:3/10}} = {{frac:30/100}} = 30%
hundred-square.why: Sara says "{{num:0.3}} is 3%". Why is she wrong? Use the square to explain.
hundred-square.model: {{num:0.3}} is 3 tenths, not 3 hundredths. Each tenth of the square is 10 small squares, so 3 tenths is 30 out of 100. Per cent means "out of 100", so {{num:0.3}} is 30%. 3% would be only 3 small squares, which is {{num:0.03}}.

feedback.too-small: Not enough. {{num:0.3}} is 3 tenths, not 3 hundredths. Each tenth is a whole column of 10 squares.
feedback.too-big: Too many. {{num:0.3}} is only 3 tenths: 3 columns out of 10.
feedback.empty: Nothing is shaded yet. Tap a small square to shade it.

fifths-to-percent.title: What percentage is {{frac:3/5}}?
fifths-to-percent.prompt: The bar is the whole thing: 100%. {{frac:3/5}} of it is shaded. First predict what percentage {{frac:3/5}} is. Then use + to split the bar into 10 parts. What percentage is each tenth?
fifths-to-percent.hint: With 10 parts, each part is 10%. How many parts are shaded?
fifths-to-percent.why: Reza wrote {{frac:3/5}} = 35%. Why is that not right?
fifths-to-percent.model: Per cent means "out of 100", so we need a denominator of 100, not the two digits written side by side. Multiply the numerator and the denominator by 20: {{frac:3/5}} = {{frac:60/100}}. The bar shows it too: 3 parts out of 5 is more than half the bar, but 35% is less than half (50%).

feedback.digits-joined: You put 3 and 5 side by side. But {{frac:3/5}} is more than half, and 35% is less than half. Split the bar into 10 parts.
feedback.tenths: {{frac:3/5}} is 6 tenths, that's right! Now give it as a percentage. Each tenth is 10%.
feedback.numerator: 3 is the number of fifths. What percentage is each fifth? Split the bar into 10 parts.
feedback.other-part: That's the percentage that is not shaded. Give the shaded percentage.
feedback.too-big: Too big. {{frac:3/5}} is less than the whole bar (100%).
feedback.too-small: Too small. Split the bar into 10 parts. Each part is 10%.

percent-of-amount.title: 30% of 50 apples
percent-of-amount.prompt: A basket holds 50 apples and 30% of them are red. The bar is all 50 apples, in 10 parts. First predict how many apples are red. Then shade 30% of the bar and type the answer.
percent-of-amount.hint: Each part is 10%. Share 50 apples between 10 parts: how many apples in each part?
percent-of-amount.success: Well done! Each part is 50 ÷ 10 = 5 apples, and 3 parts are 15 apples: 30% of 50 is 15.
percent-of-amount.why: Maryam says "30% of 50 is 20, because 50 − 30 = 20". What has she misunderstood?
percent-of-amount.model: 30% means 30 in every 100, or {{frac:3/10}} of the whole. So we split 50 into 10 equal parts and take 3 of them: 3 × 5 = 15. Taking 30 away from 50 makes no sense, because 30% is a share, not 30 apples.

feedback.wrote-percent: 30 is the percentage, not the number of apples. How many apples are in each part of the bar?
feedback.subtracted: You took 30 away from 50. But 30% means 3 parts out of 10. How many apples are in each part?
feedback.one-part: 5 apples is just one part, which is 10%. How many parts is 30%?
feedback.other-part: Those are the apples that are not red (70%). Count 3 parts.
feedback.too-big: Too many. 30% is even less than half (50%).
feedback.too-small: Too few. Work out 3 parts of the bar.
feedback.empty: Type a number: how many apples are red?

what-percent.title: 18 out of 20 as a percentage
what-percent.prompt: Ali got 18 out of 20 questions right in a test. The bar has 20 parts and 18 are shaded. First predict Ali's score as a percentage. Then use − to make the parts bigger until the bar has 10 parts.
what-percent.hint: With 10 parts, how many are shaded? Each part is 10%.
what-percent.success: Excellent! {{frac:18/20}} = {{frac:9/10}} = {{frac:90/100}}, so Ali got 90% of the questions right.
what-percent.why: Zahra got 9 out of 10 right. Who did better, Zahra or Ali? Why do percentages help us compare?
what-percent.model: Zahra also got {{frac:9/10}}, which is 90%, so they did equally well, even though 18 is more than 9. The tests had different numbers of questions. A percentage turns both scores into "out of 100", so we can compare them fairly.

feedback.wrote-score: 18 is the number of right answers. The question is: 18 out of 20 is how many out of 100?
feedback.wrong-part: That's the percentage of wrong answers (2 out of 20). Give the percentage of right answers.
feedback.wrote-missed: 2 is the number of wrong answers. Find the percentage of right answers.
feedback.too-big: Too big. Ali didn't get every question right, so it is less than 100%.
feedback.too-small: Too small. Make the bar 10 parts and count the shaded parts. Each part is 10%.
